Heritage · programme

Ramallah Preservation Project

A digital archive of Ramallah's history, begun in 2020: photographs, documents, articles and oral histories with migrants and first-generation Americans, shown at convention exhibits and with a museum partner.

Branch
Heritage · A cluster, used for life
Owning entity
Unconfirmed: the prototype says AFRP; afrp.org groups it under the Ramallah Foundation. Program Architecture asks which entity operates it.
Shape
other
Built in the Hub
Plan only

Who it's for

Anyone with materials, stories or time; submissions and interviews are welcome.

The operating year

Not stated in the record. Exhibits appear at the Convention.

The five rungs

Not stated in the record for this programme. The five rungs are hear, show up, take part, give or serve, and lead (D25).

Who runs it

The Preservation Project Committee, which gathers documents and builds exhibits. Who owns copyright and takedown decisions is open.

Money

Restricted gifts. Whose books is unconfirmed.

Hand-offs

On the Heritage cluster: no 'next' step. It wraps the family tree (items attach to tree nodes) and uses magazine back issues as archive material.

What it needs

From the Federation's strategy
  • Cultural preservation: digitisation and oral histories (2019 plan)
From the platform
  • Only a page, charter and plan exist; the archive itself is not built
  • Undecided whether the platform or a shared drive is the archive of record
  • Archive ingests only consent-classed material; print consent is its own switch

Open questions

  • Which entity operates the Preservation Project?
  • Who owns the archive's copyright and takedown decisions before member photographs go on a public site?
